name: Bwenelang
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Charpentier 1982 Atlas linguistique du Sud-Malakula wordlist entries; no grammar/phonology of Bwenelang exists per Glottolog

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir. 2020. A grammar of the Ahamb language (Vanuatu). PhD thesis, University of Waikato, sec. 2.6.1 p. 78
sources.note: Ahamb only; 'Ahamb's closest relative for which an analysis of stress patterns exists is Uluveu' -- i.e. no stress analysis exists for Bwenelang or its other SE Malakula sisters.

sources.citation: Hoback, Rachel. 2018. LLM 36 (na accretion in Banam Bay); Hoback 2024. Denggan (Banam Bay) PhD, VUW; Lynch 2020 Uripiv (comparative tables); Lynch 2014 Open Linguistics final-vowel paper; Moore 2019 Uripiv; Schaefer 2023 Ninde; Birchfield & Pearce 2021 LLM 39 Unua syllable prominence (Malakula stress survey); Tryon 1976 PL C-50; Blust 2013
sources.note: Bwenelang appears only in subgroup lists, trees, a comparative cognate column (Lynch 2020, data from Charpentier) and a moribund-language list; none says anything about its stress; Birchfield & Pearce's survey of Malakula stress statements does not include it; Tryon 1976 has no Mbwenelang wordlist.

sources.citation: Shimelman, Aviva. 2016. 'Mbwenelang (Xoli)' wordlist, ABVD record 1316 (personal communication; broad IPA)
sources.note: 181 items in broad IPA; no stress marks; no notes on prosody.

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: a new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Canberra: ANU. sec. 3.7.25 (6) Mbwenelang, p. 86; p. 71 fn 6
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: p. 86: Mbwenelang had five native speakers (Charpentier 1982a:42); 'Charpentier (1982b) provides a lengthy published lexicon for this otherwise unknown language'; Corlette unpublished vocabulary (Tryon 1972:54). p. 71 fn 6 quotes Charpentier 1982a:63 on 'the languages of the center of the island' having 'a strong tonic accent on the next to last syllable' with a destressed final vowel -- said of the Lendamboi-area interior languages, not attributed to Mbwenelang.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir, Mary Walworth & Julie Barbour. 2023. A multifaceted approach to understanding unexpected sound change: the bilabial trills of Vanuatu's Malekula Island. Diachronica 40(3): 384-432, p. 394 fn 14, p. 396
sources.note: Nothing on stress; identifies Boinelang = Vanuatu Voices 'Xoli' = Glottolog boin1237 = Charpentier's Mbwenelaŋ; no bilabial trills in the two recorded speakers.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir. 2019. [Ahamb documentation contexts]. Language Documentation and Description 16, sec. 2.2
sources.note: Nothing; only that Bwenelang was located inland of Banam Bay and identified as moribund by Charpentier (1982: 42).

sources.citation: Shimelman, Aviva et al. 2019. Sound-Comparisons 'Vanuatu' / Vanuatu Voices audio for doculect Xoli (Mbwenelang), c. 180 items, two speakers.
sources.note: Only modern primary recordings of the language; an instrumental/auditory stress analysis could be done from them, but no stress statement exists.

sources.citation: Walworth, Mary, Robert Forkel & Russell Gray (eds). Vanuatu Voices (CLLD/lexibank), doculect 'Xoli (Mbwenelang)' ID Xolimbwenelang, transcription and recordings by Aviva Shimelman (Sound-Comparisons Vanuatu, Shimelman et al. 2019)
sources.note: 177 IPA forms plus a machine-derived sound inventory; 0/177 forms carry a stress mark; no prose phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page bwen1239 'Bwenelang' (refs: Lynch 2016 subclassification x2; Campbell et al. 2022 ElCat endangerment)
sources.note: Nothing; zero descriptive references for the language.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2016. Malakula internal subgrouping: phonological evidence. Oceanic Linguistics 55(2): 399-431.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Places Bwenelang in the Southeastern Malakula subgroup using Charpentier's data; comparative sound-change evidence, unlikely to state stress but the only modern paper using the Bwenelang data.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1972. The languages of the New Hebrides: a checklist and general survey. Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-35), p. 54 (Corlette unpublished Mbwenelang vocabulary).
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: printed p. 54, entry '53; Aulua'; checklist cross-references 'Benelang see Aulua' and 'Boinelang see Aulua' on printed pp. 71-72
sources.note: Names the only other (unpublished, Corlette) vocabulary; would locate that manuscript.
sources.venue: Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-35)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 dialect page boin1237 'Boinelang' (dialect of Aulua aulu1238; no references)
sources.note: Nothing; the Vanuatu Voices Xoli (Mbwenelang) doculect is mapped to this code.

sources.citation: Charpentier, Jean-Michel. 1982a. Atlas linguistique du Sud-Malakula / Linguistic Atlas of South Malakula (Vanuatu), vol. 1 (introduction, historical migration pp. 39-48, phonological notes pp. 63-65). Langues et cultures du Pacifique 2. Paris: SELAF/CNRS/ACCT.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only work with prose on South Malakula phonology; p. 63 has an accent remark for 'the languages of the centre of the island' and p. 42 discusses Mbwenelang; only place a Mbwenelang-specific accent note could exist.

sources.citation: Charpentier, Jean-Michel. 1982b. Atlas linguistique du Sud-Malakula, vol. 2 (comparative lexicon, c. 1,500 items per language incl. Mbwenelaŋ). Paris: SELAF/CNRS/ACCT.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only published Mbwenelang lexicon; may carry accent/vowel-reduction notation (Lynch & Crowley note subscript vowel symbols for destressed finals) from which placement could be inferred.
